# requires: logging
#
# One record travelling writer -> service -> aggregator, and the question the
# chain exists to answer: who wrote this, and who handed it to me. With one
# verified field the second stamp overwrites the first and the original author
# disappears; with a chain both are on the record and both are readable.
#
# Nothing here opens a socket. `attest` applies what a receiving service does
# when the platform's attester answered with that mechanism, so the arithmetic
# of the chain is judgeable on a machine whose platform has no attester at all
# -- the same reason another layer benches an attribute at a stated strength
# rather than waiting for a peer that happens to land there.
#
# Step 5 is the forgery. A hostile writer marks its own attestation verified,
# and step 8 is the rule: it does not survive being sent, because only the party
# that ran a check may record that the check passed.
record R 0
chain R
uid R 0
author R
forge R so_peercred
chain R
send R
chain R
attest R so_peercred
chain R
author R
relay R
attest R peer_cert
chain R
author R
relay R

# expect 2: ok 0:self:claimed [LOG-I1] [LOG-I2]
# expect 3: ok uid=-1 [LOG-I11]
# expect 4: no-answer unattributed [LOG-I9]
# expect 6: ok 0:self:claimed 1:so_peercred:verified
# expect 8: ok 0:self:claimed [LOG-I5]
# expect 10: ok 0:self:claimed 1:so_peercred:verified [LOG-I6]
# expect 11: ok by=so_peercred hop=1 [LOG-I7]
# expect 12: ok by=so_peercred hop=1 [LOG-I8]
# expect 14: ok 0:self:claimed 1:so_peercred:verified 2:peer_cert:verified [LOG-I4] [LOG-I6]
# expect 15: ok by=so_peercred hop=1 [LOG-I7]
# expect 16: ok by=peer_cert hop=2 [LOG-I8]

# The disputed half, asserted by nothing. Steps 17 to 20 are a record whose
# writer attached a verified attestation and a service that then stamped it. One
# answer strips every verified attestation on accept and can never carry a
# two-hop chain; the other strips only what the sending party said about itself
# and believes a writer that attributes a stamp to a hop it did not occupy. The
# contract page names both and picks neither, so this step is judged against no
# rule.
record U 0
forge U so_peercred
attest U peer_cert
chain U

# undecided 20: no rule settles whether a verified attestation a writer attached to its own record survives a service that stamps it; the implementation shipped today strips it, which also makes the two-hop chain above unreachable through it
